title: response-merger-and-coordinated-backoff-for-parallel-tool-invocations
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Multitool scenarios where the LLM fans out parallel tool calls were exposing two UX problems: (1) duplicate/overlapping results when callers retried concurrently, and (2) downstream consumers (streaming + structured outputs) seeing interleaved injection events that broke deterministic output parsing. This PR introduces a response-merger and a coordinated retry/backoff orchestration to make parallel tool patterns ergonomic and safe.

What this changes: - response_merger: a new runtime component that accepts unordered tool results and merges them into the canonical call order before injecting into the model state. It preserves timestamps and stable tool identifiers so clients can rely on deterministic injection points. - coordinated_backoff: when multiple replicas detect transient tool failures or timeouts, replicas participate in a jittered, lease-based backoff protocol so we avoid thundering-herd retries against downstream services. - idempotency tokens: tool invocations now surface a dedupe token (derived from callset ID + tool signature) so retries are safe and side effects are not duplicated. - streaming & OpenAI-compat: updated the openai compatibility layer to expose the merged results over the same streaming chunks while keeping structured tool outputs in a stable JSON envelope (preserves previous v1 contract). - new telemetry: metrics for merged_count, reorder_events, backoff_throttled and dedupe_hits to help SRE tune thresholds.

Compatibility notes: This is opt-in behind a per-route config flag "enable_response_merger" (default false for now). The openai compat behavior remains unchanged unless the flag is enabled. Migration doc added for Dedicated/Private operators to enable at their discretion.

Testing & Validation: End-to-end harness covers: (a) parallel tool fanout with simulated downstream flakiness, (b) streaming consumers that validate JSON envelope boundaries, (c) stress test for backoff coordination under 10k/s concurrent callsets.

Related: ENG-4523 (multitool UX), ENG-4580 (backoff tuning).
commits: feat(runtime): add response_merger component and merge policy
feat(api): add enable_response_merger route config and route-level telemetry
fix(openai-compat): stream merged tool results with structured envelope
feat(runtime): coordinated backoff lease manager and jitter policy
test: add e2e harness for parallel tool injections and backoff
docs: add migration and operator guidance
review_comments: Eric Zhao: Can you clarify how the merger preserves deterministic ordering when tools return at different times? Looks good overall but need a short note in the doc about out-of-band tool timestamps.
Asha Menon: The merger sorts by callset sequence number and then by tool identifier. I've added a section in docs/migration/response_merger.md explaining tie-breakers and visibility to callers.
Lena Ortiz: Backoff lease manager looks promising. Is the lease stored in Redis or ephemeral in-process? Concerned about cross-process coordination for Dedicated nodes.
Asha Menon: Lease manager uses the same cluster lock abstraction we use for autoscaling; default implementation is Redis/etcd in private installs. Added config knobs and fallbacks.
Samir Gupta: Tests pass locally but CI flaked once on streaming chunk boundaries. Recommend adding an assertion on envelope completeness in the streaming harness.
Asha Menon: Added the envelope completeness assertion and re-ran the harness. CI green.
merge_notes: Merged after approvals from reviewers. One follow-up ticket created to make response_merger default on low-latency routes (ENG-4621).
release_notes:
- Added response_merger runtime to deterministically merge parallel tool results before injection
- Introduced coordinated retry/backoff lease mechanism to avoid thundering-herd retries
- Exposed dedupe tokens for tool idempotency
- OpenAI-compat streaming updated to deliver merged structured tool envelopes (opt-in)
- New telemetry for merged events and backoff throttles
notes: Opt-in flag used in this rollout to reduce blast radius. Operators should enable behind feature flag and monitor merged_count and dedupe_hits before enabling globally.
